aholah.title: Aholah
aholah.about: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
aholah.note: The name Ezekiel gives Samaria in his allegory of two sisters. She and Oholibah, who stands for Jerusalem, are charged with adultery for their alliances with foreign powers.

aholibah.title: Aholibah
aholibah.about: Woman living at the time of Exile and Return
aholibah.note: Ezekiel's name for Jerusalem in the allegory of the two sisters. Her sister Oholah is Samaria, and both cities' political alliances with foreign powers are painted as adultery.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

arabia.title: Arabia
arabia.note: Paul says he went away into Arabia for a time after his conversion, and in the New Testament the word covers the region south and east of Judea.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

arvad.title: Arvad
arvad.note: Arwad today, a small fortified island city off the Syrian coast. Ezekiel says Tyre hired its sailors and soldiers. It was founded by Phoenician settlers and is in the Amarna letters already, with its own fleet.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

aven.title: Aven
aven.note: A Hebrew word for nothingness, used to mock real place names. Hosea turns Bethel into Beth-aven, house of vanity, for Jeroboam's golden calf. Ezekiel 30:17 uses it for On, the Egyptian city better known as Heliopolis.

baal-meon.title: Baal-meon
baal-meon.note: It was rebuilt by Reuben, a town east of the Jordan known by several names, Beth-baal-meon and Beth-meon among them. The land around it changed hands more than once.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

beth-jeshimoth.title: Beth-jeshimoth
beth-jeshimoth.note: Israel's camp on the plains of Moab, the last before they crossed the Jordan into the promised land.

canneh.title: Canneh
canneh.note: Ezekiel lists it once among Tyre's trading partners, with Haran and Eden, somewhere in upper Mesopotamia or northern Syria. It is generally taken as the same place as Calno or Calneh.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

cherethims-2.title: Cherethims
cherethims-2.note: The people themselves, close neighbours of the Philistines and likely from Crete. Ezekiel and Zephaniah both name them in oracles of judgment.

chilmad.title: Chilmad
chilmad.note: Ezekiel lists it once among Tyre's trading partners, next to Sheba and Asshur. Some put it near Assyria. Others read the Hebrew as a phrase, not a place at all, and no location has been settled.

chittim.title: Chittim
chittim.note: Kittim was a son of Javan, and the name stretched to cover the islands and coasts of the eastern Mediterranean, Cyprus most of all. In prophecy it stands for far-off peoples who come by sea.

chub.title: Chub
chub.note: A people named once in Ezekiel's oracle against Egypt, among the allies who would fall by the sword. Many suspect a copying slip for Lub, which would make it Libya. That reading is disputed.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

cyprus-2.title: Cyprus
cyprus-2.note: Named once, in Ezekiel, and nowhere else.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

daniel.title: Daniel
daniel.about: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
daniel.note: Carried off to Babylon as a young noble of Judah and renamed by his captors, he rose to high office under three empires without giving up his faith. That refusal got him a night in the lions' den. The visions he received run to the book's last chapter.

dedan.title: Dedan
dedan.note: An Arabian trading people, known in the prophets for caravans and goods. Their ancestor Dedan was a son of Abraham through Keturah.

eden.title: Eden
eden.note: The garden where God put the first humans. A river ran out of it and split into four, the Tigris and the Euphrates among them, which is why most people look for it in the lowlands of ancient Mesopotamia. Its exact site cannot be fixed.

eden-2.title: Eden
eden-2.note: A region in northern Mesopotamia, not the garden. It sold richly worked cloth to Tyre, and the Rabshakeh named it outside Jerusalem among lands Assyria had already taken. Many identify it with Bit-Adini on the middle Euphrates, which Shalmaneser III annexed.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ezekiel.title: Ezekiel
ezekiel.about: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
ezekiel.note: A priest taken to Babylon with the first exiles. Five years in, he saw God's throne, wheels within wheels and four living creatures, and started prophesying. He acted out a lot of it, lying on his side for over a year. His valley of dry bones coming back to life is the picture of Israel restored.

gammadims.title: Gammadims
gammadims.note: Soldiers in the towers of Tyre, beside the men of Arvad, in Ezekiel's oracle. Who they were is debated: a place called Gammad, or just a word for brave warriors.

gebal.title: Gebal
gebal.note: Byblos, to the Greeks, a Phoenician port north of Beirut. Ezekiel says its craftsmen caulked the ships of Tyre. The ruins gave up the Ahiram sarcophagus, carrying one of the earliest examples of the Phoenician alphabet.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

haran.title: Haran
haran.note: Abraham's family stopped and settled here for a while on the way toward Canaan, and Abraham set out again from Haran in Genesis 12:4. The city was likely named after his brother.

helbah-2.title: Helbah
helbah-2.note: Ezekiel 27:18 actually says Helbon. Damascus sells Tyre the wine of Helbon and white wool, and Helbon is usually placed at Halbun in the hills northwest of Damascus, whose wine Strabo says the Persian kings imported.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

javan.title: Javan
javan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
javan.note: Japheth's fourth son in the table of nations. The Hebrews took his descendants to be the Ionians, the Greek world, and the prophets use Javan to mean Greece and its merchants. Modern Hebrew still calls Greece by the name.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kedar.title: Kedar
kedar.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedar.note: Ishmael's son, and the father of a desert tribe known for dark tents and good archers. Poets use Kedar for far-off wilderness living, and the Song of Solomon uses it for dark beauty.

koa.title: Koa
koa.note: Ezekiel names Koa once, with Shoa and Pekod, among the peoples coming with Babylon against Jerusalem. Many scholars take it to be Gutium, a land east of the Tigris that turns up in Sumerian, Babylonian and Assyrian records.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

lud.title: Lud
lud.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
lud.note: Shem's son. His people are usually taken to be the Lydians of Asia Minor. Some later passages may mean a people in Africa instead.

mesech.title: Mesech
mesech.note: Japheth's son, and the people who came from him. The prophets pair Meshech again and again with Tubal as far-off, warlike nations of the north.

migdol.title: Migdol
migdol.note: "Tower," a fortified point on Egypt's northeastern border. One Migdol is on Israel's route to the crossing of the sea. Jeremiah names a Migdol where Jewish refugees settled in Egypt, and Ezekiel's "from Migdol to Syene" means the whole length of the country.

minnith.title: Minnith
minnith.note: Jephthah's victory over the Ammonites ran as far as this town. Ezekiel lists wheat from Minnith among the goods Judah sold to Tyre. It stood on the tableland east of the Jordan, somewhere near Heshbon and Rabbah.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

nebuchadnezzar.title: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuchadnezzar.note: King of Babylon. He destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off, and the Bible still calls him the tool God used to judge his people. Daniel tells how, after boasting of his greatness, he went mad and lived like an animal for seven years, until he gave God the glory and got his throne back.

no.title: No
no.note: Nahum points to the fall of No, the Hebrew name for the Egyptian city of Thebes, as a warning to Nineveh that no city is too strong for God's judgment.

noph.title: Noph
noph.note: Memphis, under its Hebrew name, which several prophets use when they speak of Egypt's coming judgment.

pannag.title: Pannag
pannag.note: A trade good Judah and Israel sold to Tyre, listed with wheat and honey. What it actually was, nobody knows.

pathros.title: Pathros
pathros.note: Upper Egypt. Jewish refugees fled there, and the prophets name it among the places God promised to gather his scattered people back from.

pekod.title: Pekod
pekod.note: Not a person. Pekod is a tribal or regional name in southern Babylonia, the Puqudu of Assyrian and Babylonian records, and both Jeremiah and Ezekiel bring it into their oracles against Babylon.

persia.title: Persia
persia.note: The empire that took Babylon under Cyrus. Unlike the empires before it, Persia let the exiled Jews go home and rebuild their temple, and Ezra keeps the decree.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phut.title: Phut
phut.note: A son of Ham in the table of nations. The prophets tie his descendants to northern Africa, likely ancient Libya, and keep listing them among the hired soldiers in other people's armies.

pi-beseth.title: Pi-beseth
pi-beseth.note: Ezekiel says its young men will fall by the sword. The Greeks called it Bubastis, a city in the eastern Nile Delta and the center of worship for the cat goddess Bastet.

raamah-2.title: Raamah
raamah-2.note: Named once, in Ezekiel, and nowhere else.

rabbah.title: Rabbah
rabbah.note: Capital of Ammon. David's army besieged it, and Uriah died in that siege, put where the fighting was worst on David's orders.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

senir.title: Senir
senir.note: The Amorite name for Mount Hermon. Ezekiel mentions its fir trees, which went into the ships of Tyre.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

shoa.title: Shoa
shoa.note: Not a man but a people or district, named with Pekod and Koa in Ezekiel 23:23 among the lovers who will turn on Oholibah.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sin.title: Sin
sin.note: Israel crossed the Wilderness of Sin after leaving Egypt, and when the people complained of hunger this is where the manna and the quail first came.

syene.title: Syene
syene.note: The southern edge of Egypt, at modern Aswan by the first cataract of the Nile. Ezekiel uses Migdol and Syene the way we would say from one end of the country to the other.

tahapanes.title: Tahapanes
tahapanes.note: An Egyptian fort town on the eastern edge of the Nile delta. After Gedaliah was murdered the refugees ran there and took Jeremiah with them against his advice, and he said there that Nebuchadnezzar would set his throne over stones buried at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

togarmah.title: Togarmah
togarmah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
togarmah.note: Gomer's son and Japheth's grandson. Ezekiel's people of Togarmah trade horses and mules, from somewhere in eastern Asia Minor.

tubal.title: Tubal
tubal.note: In the prophets Tubal is a far northern people, usually named with Meshech, trading and making war. The name goes back to a son of Japheth.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uzal-2.title: Uzal
uzal-2.note: Named once, in Ezekiel, and nowhere else.

vedan.title: Vedan
vedan.note: Ezekiel lists it among Tyre's trading partners, next to Javan, bringing wrought iron, cassia and calamus. The Hebrew is hard here, and some read Vedan, a place in Arabia, rather than Dan.

zoan.title: Zoan
zoan.note: Tanis, to the Greeks, a city in the Nile delta that was once Egypt's capital. Numbers says it was built seven years after Hebron. The psalmist puts the plagues in the field of Zoan.
